note: Readings from al-Khaṣāʾiṣ (khasais-*): every contradiction tools/grammar_audit.js listed on the new packages, judged by the line. The first run listed 16; four were the author's and were corrected in the scripts (listed under «corrected»). Second run: 13 records on the shelf (two for the same token under two jumla rules), all judged here: E = the engine is wrong by the books, C = both readings are allowed, undecided = left for the hoca (the vowel is unwritten in the text).

records.why: «عَلِمْتَ» answers «إِذَا سَمِعْتَ»; «أَبُوهُ» is the doer inside the quoted example «وَشَكَرَ سَعِيدًا أَبُوهُ», not a mubtadaʾ owed a predicate — the engine reads across the quotation.
«عَلِمْتَ» answers «إِذَا سَمِعْتَ»; «أَبُوهُ» is the doer inside the quoted example «وَشَكَرَ سَعِيدًا أَبُوهُ», not a mubtadaʾ owed a predicate — the engine reads across the quotation.
«لَاسْتَبْهَمَ» opens with the lām of the answer of «لَوْ»; a clause carrying that lām is the answer, not an adjective of «وَاحِدًا».
«سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَى» is the glorification put in between «قَالَ اللهُ» and the quoted verse; the maqūl is the verse «وَإِذَا مَرُّوا …», which the line says.
«الْيَحْيَوْنَ» is the sound plural of the maqṣūr name يَحْيَى (the alif dropped, the fatha kept), in raf' by the waw; the engine does not see a sound plural in ـَوْنَ and reads a damma.

whether كُمَّثْرَى takes tanwin turns on whether its alif is of attachment (the singular كُمَّثْرَاة suggests so) or of the feminine; the text leaves the vowel of the rā unwritten and the point is in the hoca's list.
«فَكُلُّ لَفْظٍ مُسْتَقِلٍّ»: «لَفْظٍ» is the second term of «كُلُّ» and is itself not annexed (مُسْتَقِلٍّ is its adjective), so it keeps its tanwin.

the e-text's «يسميه النحويين» is kept as printed (no witness found) and the line says the doer wants «النَّحْوِيُّونَ»; the engine's nasb object is impossible — «يُسَمِّي» already has its two objects, the هاء and «الْجُمَلَ».
«لَبِّ» is built on kasra like أَمْسِ and غَاقِ, as the editor's note on the line says (al-Lisān); a built word takes no tanwin of declension.

«أُفِّ» without tanwin (definite) and «أُفٍّ» with the tanwin of indefiniteness are both said of the noun-verbs; the same bāb cites them both ways — «صَهْ، وَمَهْ» bare and «صَهٍ وَإِيهٍ» with tanwin.

cite.ar: وصه، ومه، ورويد … من نحو صهٍ وإيهٍ

records.why: «أَوَّهْ» is a built sound-word on sukun (one of its lexicon forms), quoted in the list; the engine declines it as a conjoined noun.
«تَوَاضُعٌ وَاصْطِلَاحٌ، لَا وَحْيٌ وَتَوْقِيفٌ»: لَا conjoins after an affirmed predicate and «وَحْيٌ» follows «تَوَاضُعٌ» in raf'; there is no genus-لَا with its own predicate here.
«وَتَتَحَمَّلُ لِذٰلِكَ مَشَاقَّهُ»: «مَشَاقَّهُ» is the object of «تَتَحَمَّلُ»; «لِذٰلِكَ» is a closed jarr phrase and cannot take a second term.
